applies_to: Swegon GOLD air handling units of generation C and D (RX, PX, CX and SD versions, built about 2010-2013) running program version 6.08 or later.
summary: GOLD generation C/D air handlers have a BACnet IP driver built into the unit controller (program version 6.08), acting as a B-ASC; no gateway is needed. The list covers fan airflows, pressures, levels and power, temperatures and regulator setpoints, heat exchanger and coil data, accessory functions (Xzone, ReCO2, AYC, MIRU, Blue Box, steam humidifier), time and year channels, one binary input per alarm and info number, and calibration commands. The BMS starts, stops and selects speed through one analog value.
notes: Taken from GB.BACnet480.121017 (pp3-49). Only the first page of each object section has a text layer; the rest are images, read by OCR and checked against zoomed page renders. Instances missing from the OCR were filled from the printed sequence and the pages were checked by eye where they jumped.
Access follows the section headings: Analog Inputs and Binary Inputs read-only, Analog Values and Binary Values read/write.

The guide prints only the first and last objects of two long ranges: BI 48-50 and BI 247 (Alarm number 1-3 and 200) and BI 248-250 and BI 347 (Info number 1-3 and 100). Going by those rows, Alarm number n is BI 47+n and Info number n is BI 247+n; only the printed rows are listed here.
Instances not printed in the guide (AV 55, AV 96, AV 123, BI 44-47, BV 4-6, BV 17, BV 20) are left out.
The Misc column marks the program version that added an object (PV 5.10 to 6.08); it is shown in the description as "from PV x". Descriptions keep the printed Min/Max range.
This is an older generation than the GOLD E list (different instance numbers); Compact / GOLD LP units have their own list.
AV 263 is printed as 'Year channel 6 start hour.' although it sits in the channel 5 block; the name is kept as printed.

integration.summary: Command the unit with AV 174 Communication operation mode (0 = Auto lets the time channels run it; 1-4 force stop or low/high speed) and read back AI 84 Operation mode 1 plus the low/high speed BIs. Adjust the main temperature setpoints (AV 40 supply, AV 41 extract/room) and the low/high speed airflow or pressure setpoints, and monitor BI 5/BI 6 for A/B alarms with BV 0 to reset. Page 3 of the guide lists these as the key points.

minimum_points.name: Communication operation mode
minimum_points.why: BMS stop / low / high speed command (0 = Auto)

minimum_points.name: Operation mode 1
minimum_points.why: Actual operating mode and what stopped the unit

minimum_points.name: Outdoor temperature
minimum_points.why: Outdoor air temp measured by the unit, °C

integration.enable: AV 174 Communication operation mode: 0=Auto (normal stop when the time channels are deactivated), 1=Communication stop 1, 2=Communication low speed, 3=Communication high speed, 4=Communication stop 2 (PV 5.00 or later; intermittent night heat and morning boost still work). AI 84 Operation mode 1 shows whether the unit is stopped or running from the hand terminal, an external input, communication or a time/year channel.
integration.remote_sensors: Room temperature can come from the BMS: set AV 200 EA/Room temperature external func. to 2 (Communication) and write AV 201. Outdoor temperature works the same with AV 202 = 2 and AV 203. AV 204 sets the timeout for these communicated temperatures.
setup: BACnet IP only; the device is a B-ASC. Swegon also publishes a BACnet PICS and an EDE file for GOLD.
Device instance and IP settings are not given in this document.
gotchas: Setpoints are split by low and high speed (e.g. AV 0/1 SA airflow, AV 8/9 SA duct pressure); write the one for the active speed.
BV 42-73 start pressure-sensor zero calibration or set it to manual mode; do not write them from routine BMS logic.
Many objects only mean something when the related accessory or heat exchanger type (RX/PX/CX/SD) is installed.
The time channel status objects (AV 130, 135, ... 165) use 0-10 for low speed days and 16-26 for high speed days.
